title: A diferencia de: al contrario de, en contraste con

sections.content: A diferencia de (unlike, in contrast to) sets up an explicit contrast between two things -- it's followed directly by a noun phrase, not a clause. Use it whenever you want to highlight how one case departs from another. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Chile, a diferencia de la mayoría de sus vecinos, mantuvo durante toda la década un crecimiento económico sostenido y una notable reducción de la pobreza.
items.english: Chile, unlike most of its neighbors, maintained sustained economic growth and a notable reduction in poverty throughout the decade.

items.spanish: A diferencia de lo que prometían sus arquitectos, la apertura económica no garantizaba por sí sola ni estabilidad política ni bienestar social.
items.english: Unlike what its architects promised, economic opening alone did not guarantee either political stability or social wellbeing.

items.spanish: La región terminó la década siendo, a diferencia de otras zonas del mundo en desarrollo, una de las más desiguales del planeta.
items.english: The region ended the decade being, unlike other developing regions of the world, one of the most unequal on the planet.

items.spanish: Ese contraste, a diferencia de la promesa inicial de que el crecimiento beneficiaría a todos por igual, dejó sembrado el terreno para los cambios políticos siguientes.
items.english: That contrast, unlike the initial promise that growth would benefit everyone equally, laid the groundwork for the political changes that followed.

sections.content: A diferencia de takes a noun phrase (a diferencia de Chile, a diferencia de lo que prometían) -- never a full conjugated clause on its own. Compare it with mientras que, which does introduce a full clause of contrast.
